$comment: Registry of every gate exemption in this repository. Consumed by
scripts/tests/test_gate_exemption_registry.py.
MEMBERSHIP IS DERIVED, REASONS ARE AUTHORED. scripts/exemption_discovery.py finds
every exemption surface in the tree -- Python constants by name AND by the prose of
their attached comment, Make variables, shell variables, linter config keys and JSON
baselines -- and the meta-test fails in BOTH directions: a surface that is not
registered here, and an entry here whose surface has vanished. This file is itself a
list, and the whole subject of the change that created it is that hand-maintained
lists go stale, so only the judgement in it is hand-maintained.
WHY IT EXISTS. Four exemption lists stated a premise that was false for at least one
member, and in each case the false member was the one the gate most needed to see.
Every one was the same bug: ONE justification attached to a SET, where the
justification is a property of individual members. Read in aggregate -- 'does this
reason hold broadly?' -- all four pass. So the rule this registry encodes is that a
reason answers for one member, and a premise that can be computed is computed.
FIELDS.
kind      exemption        a real carve-out: members escape an assertion
enforced-universe the list IS the enforced set; the risk is omission
prune             build output / gitignored local work, not a carve-out
fixture           test data that matched the vocabulary; turns nothing off
capability        a runtime allow/deny grant, not a gate
turnsOff  what stops being asserted for a member (required, non-empty)
premise   the name of a predicate in scripts/tests/gate_premises.py that the owning
gate evaluates PER MEMBER, or JUDGEMENT when there is genuinely nothing to
compute. JUDGEMENT is not an escape from scrutiny: a reason is then
required, and the ratchets still apply.
reason    required when premise is JUDGEMENT
ratchet   what makes the exemption finite even where the premise cannot be checked:
non-vacuity (it must shield something), count-pinned (it shields only as
many sites as were audited), universe-closure (nothing may sit outside
both sets), staleness (a dead entry fails), prune-meta-test (deferred to
test_repo_walk_guards_prune_local_work.py), or none
ratchetGap required when ratchet is none: what is consequently unprotected. These
are the honest residuals of this mechanism, and they are enumerable --
which is the point. An unmeasured gap is how this class started.
crossReferences  other entries that must be audited with this one. Two exemptions
pointed at each other in comments and two independent surveys audited one
half and never followed the pointer.
premiseWiring  'pending' on an entry whose premise IS computable but whose gate
does not yet call the predicate. It requires a reason and is counted:
MAX_PENDING_WIRING in the meta-test may shrink and not grow. This state
exists so that 'computable but unchecked' is distinguishable from
'nothing to compute' -- collapsing the two into JUDGEMENT is how a
checkable premise stops being checked.
predicateConsidered  {predicate: why it does not settle the question}. Required when
a JUDGEMENT reason invokes the subject of a predicate that exists --
nested stacks, the publisher's build, an installer manifest, test
collection. See the LIMIT below for what this does and does not buy.
THE LIMIT OF JUDGEMENT AND ratchetGap, STATED PLAINLY.
Both are escape hatches, and a mechanism that pretends otherwise would be the defect
it is meant to fix. So, precisely what each is worth:
* A JUDGEMENT reason cannot be checked. No test reads a sentence. What IS checked is
narrower and is the failure mode that actually occurred four times: a reason that
RESTATES IN PROSE a fact this tree can compute. If the wording invokes a
predicate's subject, the entry must name that predicate or set it aside in
predicateConsidered with a sentence. That is a lint on this file, not a claim about
the world -- it never asks whether a template is a nested stack, only whether an
author who wrote 'nested stack' engaged with the predicate that answers it.
* An author can still write a premise the vocabulary does not recognise, and get
JUDGEMENT plus ratchetGap for it. Nothing here stops that, and nothing here
pretends to. The bound on it is quantitative rather than semantic:
MAX_UNRATCHETED and MAX_PENDING_WIRING may shrink and not grow, so the cost of
reaching for the hatch is a deliberate, visible edit to a pinned number in a test
-- which is a review moment, not a check.
* PREDICATE_DOMAIN_WORDING is therefore the thing to keep current. It is the only
part of this mechanism that degrades silently: a new predicate whose subject is
not listed there can be restated in prose with nothing objecting. Adding a
predicate to gate_premises.PREDICATES means adding its wording there too.
* What none of this covers: whether a JUDGEMENT reason is TRUE. That remains a
reviewer's job, and it is why every reason here is required to state a fact about
this tree rather than restate AWS behaviour from memory -- the rule
TRANSPORT_CONTROL_EXEMPT states in its own comment, generalised.
memberKind  What ONE member names: "path", "deployable path" (a CloudFormation
template or a Lambda source tree), "CloudFormation logical id", "Bedrock
model id", "make target", and so on. Required, and not inferred: it
decides which predicates can possibly apply. A "deployable path" exemption
may NOT be pure JUDGEMENT -- whether the parent deploys it and whether one
publish run builds it are computable, and all four original defects
asserted one of them in prose. The rule stops at deployable paths on
purpose: demanding the same of a documentation link-check exemption would
produce boilerplate nobody reads, and a registry that asks for judgement
on noise gets rubber-stamped.
issues    Optional. Issue or PR numbers already addressing this exemption, so a reader
can tell a known-and-tracked carve-out from an unexamined one. Absent means
'nobody is working on it', which is itself information.

lib/idp_common_pkg/tests/unit/config/tes.memberKind: the name of a sub-section under the `extraction` key of a resolved system-defaults document
lib/idp_common_pkg/tests/unit/config/tes.turnsOff: nothing. It is the complete set of `extraction` sub-sections the BDA pattern's resolved defaults may hold, and the test compares it for EQUALITY, so a member being in it is what makes that member required rather than what excuses it. A third sub-section appearing under that key fails the same assertion.
lib/idp_common_pkg/tests/unit/config/tes.reason: Discovered through the prose route, on a comment saying the LLM extraction settings are 'deliberately absent' from the BDA pattern -- which reads as an exclusion decision and is instead the fact being asserted. The v0.6 refactor moved per-field confidence and bounding-box geometry under `extraction`, so the BDA pattern has to compose those two modules while still omitting the extraction module itself; this constant names what that leaves under the key, and the assertion is equality in both directions, which is the closure. There is no member the set omits by choice and no per-member fact to compute, because the comparison is against what the real loader resolves rather than against an authored inventory: a module that added a third sub-section under `extraction`, or one of these two ceasing to be inherited, fails there without anyone editing this file. What a reviewer should check instead is that the equality is real -- add a sub-section to base-confidence.yaml and watch it fail. Registered rather than reworded, because rewording a comment to slip past discovery is the failure this registry exists to prevent, and 'not a carve-out at all' is a decision the registry is built to record.

pyrightconfig.json::exclude.turnsOff: basedpyright type checking for the listed paths
pyrightconfig.json::exclude.reason: Generated, vendored and build-output trees. Members split by why they are here rather than sharing one reason, and every category is now either computed per member or carries its own record. The bare cache and artifact directory names (**/build, **/dist, **/.venv, **/.aws-sam, **/cdk.out, **/node_modules, **/__pycache__) are bare on purpose, since such a directory is build output wherever it sits -- and that claim is computed rather than asserted: each leaf must satisfy vcs_ignored_build_output, which is what stops `**/<name>` becoming the spelling that excludes anything without a reason (**/notebooks has the same shape and does not qualify). The two named paths under feature-platform/idp-data-generator are specific staged trees, each with its own reason and computed premise in scripts/tests/test_pyright_config.py::STAGED_BUILD_OUTPUT_EXEMPT. notebooks/**/*.ipynb is a scope decision recorded in TYPECHECK_SCOPE_EXCLUSIONS in the same file. **/*-converted.py is a generated filename shape recorded in GENERATED_ARTIFACT_EXCLUSIONS there. What makes the array as a whole trustworthy is not this reason but the closure tests around it: every include path must exist, every first-party distribution must be covered, no exclude may shadow an include, every tracked .py must be reached, the walk must reach nothing an ignore rule covers, and every exclude entry must fall in one of those four categories or fail.

The call lives in the sibling entry's gate, scripts/tests/test_pyright_config.py, which parametrises it over every bare `**/<name>` pattern in this array -- that is the cross-reference below, and it is why the two entries point at each other.

ruff.toml::format.exclude.turnsOff: `ruff format --check` for the 184 named files, so they are neither reformatted by `make format` nor failed by the format gate
ruff.toml::format.exclude.reason: The files `ruff format` had never been run over, because the trees holding them were excluded by bare name before issue #975. Paying one down rewrites the whole file, so the sweep was deliberately left out of the change that closed #975: five of the seven branches then open were editing 42 of these files and a repo-wide reformat would have conflicted with all five. scripts/check_account_ids.py::BINARY_EXT.turnsOff: reading one file's contents at all, for a file in a non-text format
scripts/check_account_ids.py::BINARY_EXT.reason: WHAT IS RATCHETED HERE IS THE SET OF EXTENSIONS, NOT A COUNT OF SKIPPED FILES. The gate decides per file whether contents are text by looking for a NUL byte in the first 8 KiB, and this set records which formats are allowed to answer yes; the closure check fails on any skipped file whose extension is not named. Choosing extensions over a count is deliberate: a count would red-line the branch on the next sample PNG, which is friction for no safety, whereas what genuinely needs to fail is a file the gate STOPS being able to read -- a text file that gains a NUL byte in its first 8 KiB, or a new tree in an undeclared binary format. Both of those the closure catches; a hundred more images it does not. No file total is recorded here because it moves with every merge; the skipped set today is almost entirely images and PDFs, and `--summary` prints the live count. Whether a format is text is not something this tree computes, which is why the membership is authored. The member set is now pinned by test_the_not_measured_list_has_not_grown, so growing this list is a named failure rather than an exemption that takes effect the moment it is written.

scripts/coverage_debt.json::coverage_deb.reason: Not a carve-out: the opposite. This is the ENFORCED set -- every tracked idp_common module and the coverage it must not fall below. It is discovered by the registry scanner because its filename matches the *_debt.json pattern the lint-debt baseline established, and it is registered so that similarity is recorded rather than mistaken for an exclusion list. Generated by `python3 scripts/check_coverage_debt.py --write`. Hand-editing is confined to ONE case, and only that one: adding a single entry for a new file at the percentage a clean run measured for it, which is what a change introducing a file has to do to keep the gate closed. Everything else comes from `--write`. The carve-out exists because `--write` rewrites EVERY recorded percentage from the current report, so on a tree where an unrelated file's real coverage has drifted down since its floor was recorded, running it inside an unrelated change lowers that floor too -- measured at three files on the tree where this was written (0.72, 0.41 and 0.03 points, each reproducible on an independent run, so real drift rather than noise, and each inside the gate's own 1.0-point tolerance so leaving the floor high blocks nobody). The script's own docstring gives the reason: re-recording on every improvement is how a file whose coverage had fallen gets re-recorded along with it. What is NOT permitted is editing an existing number by hand, in either direction. Nothing enforces that boundary -- no test can see a hand-edit -- so it is a reviewer's check, and an added line must state the measured value in the pull request that adds it. test_coverage_debt.py::test_the_recorded_baseline_is_not_empty is the non-vacuity ratchet, and it exists because the first version of the generator silently recorded zero files and reported success.

patterns/unified/tests/test_workflow_tra.turnsOff: the requirement that a task state permitted to invoke a Bedrock model retry TransientError, for five named states

Both halves have to land per state and neither is in this change; none of the five handlers swallows, so what is lost meanwhile is the retry rather than the diagnosis. Each entry carries what is specific to that handler -- OCRStep calls a model only on the bedrock backend, ClassificationStep once per page, SummarizationStep once over the whole document at the end of the pipeline, EvaluationStep only through the LLM-judge comparators, and RecordEvaluationFailure on a deliberately shorter transient tier because it runs on the failure path -- and the gate asserts those reasons are distinct, because length plus a substring would accept five identical strings. Whether a handler SHOULD convert is a judgement about its failure modes, which no predicate computes; what the gate computes is membership of the universe, from the ASL Resource placeholder through DefinitionSubstitutions to the granted IAM actions of the target function and of any role it references.
patterns/unified/tests/test_workflow_tra.ratchetGap: The predicate answers 'permitted to invoke a model', not 'does invoke one', so an entry can be justified by a grant its handler never uses. It reads actions out of Action: position rather than out of the block's raw text, which is what stops an ARN's wildcard REGION (arn:<partition>:bedrock:*::foundation-model/*, twelve of them here) being read as a bedrock:* action -- there is no such action in this template, and reading one put a data-automation-only function in the universe. What remains loose is the action pattern itself: any future action whose name begins InvokeModel or Converse would qualify regardless of what it does. Over-inclusion is the safe direction for a closure. The closure is also one-directional by design: a state that is NOT Bedrock-capable may still list TransientError legitimately (PolicyClassificationStep does, for DynamoDB and S3 transients), so nothing here detects a listing that is no longer needed.

Makefile::COVERAGE_CICD_SKIP.reason: Discovered by name: the fragment `SKIP` is in the discovery vocabulary, and it matching here is the mechanism working rather than a false positive -- a variable that removes a tree from a coverage producer is exactly the shape this registry governs, whatever its intent.
